WetBond is a new name. The chemistry isn't.

Circa 2010Saved a retail slab emitting more than twice the moisture conventional coatings tolerate. The case study is below.
2021Selected as one of two top performers in an Ohio DOT and University of Cincinnati bridge study (report FHWA/OH-2021-13).

allowedClaimsDebtDeltas.before:
Why we can warrant the bond for life

Coatings stick to concrete. WetBond bonds into the concrete.

Paints, epoxies and membranes hold on mechanically: they grip the surface texture of the concrete. Moisture keeps arriving behind them, and vapor pressure and crystallizing minerals push that grip apart over time. That’s why coatings carry short warranties.

WetBond works differently. It travels into the concrete and reacts there, forming chemical bonds with the concrete itself.

So the bond lasts as long as the concrete does. That’s how we define lifetime.

Mechanical bond (coatings)Chemical bond (WetBond)
Where it holdsOn the surfaceInside the concrete
How it holdsGrips surface textureReacts and bonds with the concrete
What breaks itVapor pressure and salts working behind the filmOnly the concrete itself failing
Warranty we give—Lifetime bond warranty

What “lifetime” means: for as long as the treated concrete or masonry is in place. The bond warranty covers treated surfaces peeling, lifting, flaking off or losing their bond. It doesn’t cover the concrete itself failing, such as new cracks from structural movement, impact, or removal and replacement. Full terms are provided before you sign.
